previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis was admitted for a moderate flare characterized by epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and low-grade fever. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, IV pain control including a Dilaudid PCA, and antiemetics. Due to slow improvement and moderate malnutrition, TPN was restarted and advanced to goal. Blood cultures, chest X-ray, and urinalysis showed no infection, and fevers resolved spontaneously. Her pain gradually improved to baseline, and she transitioned to oral hydromorphone while her fentanyl patch was reduced to 100 mcg/hr. She was advanced to a soft diet, managed for constipation, and continued on omeprazole twice daily for worsening GERD, with plans for outpatient EGD. She remained mentally clear, afebrile, and ambulatory, and was discharged home with TPN support, home health, and follow-up arranged.

radiology_notes.text:
MRCP

INDICATION:  ___ woman with recent prolonged admission and recurrent
abdominal pain.  Currently on TPN due to recurrent pancreatitis.

Comparison was performed with previous MRCP study from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired on 1.5 Tesla
magnet including dynamic 3D imaging obtained prior, during and after
uneventful intravenous administration of 0.1 mmol/kg (15 cc) of
gadolinium-DTPA.  

Multiplanar 2D and 3D reconstructions and subtraction images were essential in
demonstrating the below findings.

FINDINGS:  The liver demonstrates normal signal intensity, apart from the
single lesion in segment VI of the liver, which demonstrates high-signal
intensity on T2-weighted images, with nearly homogeneous arterial and
portovenous enhancement, findings consistent with hemangioma.  There is no
evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  Status post
cholecystectomy.

Pancreas demonstrates mild atrophy with normal signal intensity in the body
and tail of the pancreas, but decreased signal intensity of the parenchyma in
the head and uncinate process.  Further noted irregularity of the main
pancreatic duct with a number of dilated side branches in the body and tail of
pancreas (series 5, image 21 and series 7, image 1).

Adrenals are unremarkable bilaterally.  Kidneys are within normal limits apart
from a single simple cortical cyst in the upper pole of the right kidney. 
Spleen is within normal limits.  There is no evidence of retroperitoneal or
mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  Visualized bowel loops are unremarkable.  Bone
marrow signal is within normal limits.

Multiplanar 2D and 3D reconstructions and subtraction images were essential in
demonstrating the above findings.


IMPRESSION:
1.  Slight decreased signal intensity in the head and uncinate process of the
pancreas, which may correspond to chronic pancreatitis.

2.  Irregular contour of the non-dilated main pancreatic duct, more prominent
in the head and neck of the pancreas, along with mildly dilated side branches
in the body and tail of pancreas, unchanged from prior study, consistent with
chronic pancreatitis.

3.  No evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.

4.  Unchanged hemangioma in the liver.
